newsitem.title: USA: NYC Councilman wants plastic boardwalks, benches.
newsitem.headline: NYC Councilman wants plastic boardwalks, benches.

text.p: A New York City Council member on Monday said he would introduce a bill calling on the parks department to use plastic for boardwalks and benches instead of hardwoods cut from rain forests.

The bill aims to tighten loopholes in a 1991 state law restricting the use of rain forest hardwoods, said Marcel Van Ooyen, a legislative aide to A. Gifford Miller, a Democrat who represents the upper East Side of Manhattan.
Miller plans to unveil the bill on Tuesday.

However, Marc Matsil, the chief of the natural resources group at the city's Department of Parks and Recreation, said plastic, recyclable materials at present were too flammable and not strong enough for boardwalks. He said plastics could not support emergency vehicles.

Matsil said the Tiffany Street pier in the South Bronx, which the city's General Services Department built from such material, was set ablaze about a year and a half ago after being struck by lightning.

"It would be wonderful to use recylcable plastic," he later added. "I think it would be the way to go, but not until it can support a) durablity and b) not be a danger that the public will be burnt to a crisp."

In prepared remarks, Miller said the bill would ban the city from buying any timber from rain forests unless it was certified to have been cut in way that safeguarded the forest's future. Guidelines for sustainable growth set out by the Forest Stewardship Council, based in Oaxaca, Mexico, would have to be met.
Estimates of how much rain forest hardwoods were not immediately available. Van Ooyen said the city buys Ipe wood, which is grown in Brazil, Paraguay and Argentina.
But the Parks Department official said that the city only buys rainforest timber from two mills that already meet these guidelines.
